2. This is second application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail to the applicant as he has been arrested on 14.01.2023 in connection with Crime No.13/2023 registered at Police Station Lahar, District Bhind for the offence punishable under Sections 376(a)(b), 511, 354, 354(a) of IPC and Section 9(m) and 10 of POCSO Act.
2.1

Applicant's first application filed under Section 439 of CrPC was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 16.06.2023 passed by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.24286/2023 with liberty to file a fresh application after recording of statement of complainant, i.e., mother of prosecutrix.

sentences.text: Prosecution case, in brief, is that, on 14.01.2023 at about 12:00 hours, when complainant's minor daughter aged about 11 years was playing outside the house, at that time, the applicant gave her 100 rupees to bring biscuit and when the prosecutrix went inside the applicant's house to give biscuit to him, then the applicant closed the doors of the house from inside, took off his underwear, showed his private part to her and told her to do indecent act, then she refused to do so, thereafter, applicant held her both hands and made her sit on the bed and when she started crying, then her younger sister knocked the doors.
Thereafter, the prosecutrix came to her house and narrated the aforesaid incident to her mother.

4 . Learned counsel for the applicant submits that after dismissal of applicant's first application,
statement of the prosecutrix as well as her mother complainant along with her father have been recorded. Prosecutrix denied the allegations alleged against the applicant.
All the material witnesses have been examined and their statements have been recorded.
Trial will still take time to conclude.
The applicant is in custody since 14.01.2023.
Under these circumstances, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer and submits that allegations alleged against the applicant are heinous in nature, therefore, he is not entitled for grant of bail.

6. Heard the learned counsel for both the parties.
7.

Having considered the rival submissions, material pointed out by the learned counsel for the applicant, so also the fact that material witnesses have been examined, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7.1 It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of, accordingly.
Certified copy, as per rules.

(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE Abhi Kalyan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123946372/
